title: The mechanical clock
summary: The first mechanical clocks were probably made in the late 1200s. What makes a mechanical clock is its escapement, which ticks in a steady rhythm and lets the gears move in small jumps. The first was the verge and foliot, driven by a heavy stone. A chronicle at Dunstable Priory in England records in 1283 that 'we made a clock over the pulpit'.

uncertainty.note: Mechanical clocks emerged in northern Europe around the 1280s; Robert the Englishman noted in 1271 that craftsmen were still attempting uniform weight-driven rotation, while the Annals of Dunstable Priory record an operational horologium above the pulpit in 1283.

importance.justification: The verge-and-foliot escapement created the first all-mechanical oscillatory timekeeper, replacing continuous water clocks with uniform mechanical hours and transforming labour discipline, astronomy, and European technology.
